# Linux ALSA native ownership amendment

This same-version CPAL 0.18.2 source amendment adds a Linux-specific, fallible PCM close contract. It does not change the upstream ALSA/BSD Drop route or claim hardware acceptance.

## Provenance

CPAL's published archive remains 0.18.2, SHA-256 `6f02e8d0327b42d3e2e4ab2119af397344eb9fc54a34bf0ddeaa1277af8681f1`, upstream commit `e1612d5d98152f8dc2a62e1b51ef7cbf4f7f26b7`. The Apache-2.0 license and original manifest/source attribution remain present.

The companion `vendor/alsa` is the complete published alsa-rs 0.11.0 archive, SHA-256 `812947049edcd670a82cd5c73c3661d2e58468577ba8489de58e1a73c04cbd5d`, with only `src/pcm.rs` amended to expose consuming checked `snd_pcm_close` and the existing native PCM-type query. The consuming method accepts only native zero as success and preserves every other raw status; a positive out-of-contract status is retained with handle consumption unproved. Its original manifest, lockfile, licenses, source and `.orig` remain present. The Apache-2.0/MIT license expression is unchanged. alsa-sys remains registry 0.4.0, checksum `ad7569085a265dd3f607ebecce7458eaab2132a84393534c95b18dcbc3f31e04`; no dependency version or build hook is added.

## Receipt and failure boundaries

Before any PCM open, a finite process registry owns a supervisor, which owns the actual native control thread. That control owner holds partial configuration, the PCM, transfer-thread join handle, pipe ends and context. Stream Drop only revokes callback/native admission with atomics. Play/pause/query operations run on the retained control owner. Callback and control bodies, captured values and their TLS must really join before Released is published. A blocked native call or destructor remains owned and observers may time out. Final supervisor join has no hard OS scheduling guarantee and close/drain observation is restricted to a retained non-UI, non-Tokio worker.

ALSA application callbacks run in a retained Rust thread, not across a C callback ABI. Rust panic/unwind behavior is preserved. An exit guard revokes admission during unwind; the actual callback JoinHandle returns the original opaque panic payload, held without formatting or waiter destruction. Callback/control/TLS panic is a non-successful retained failure. There is no signal, kill, detached closer, destructor-as-receipt or raw-pointer retry.

The documented libasound `snd_pcm_close` contract returns zero for successful close. Independently bound primary 1.2.2, 1.2.11 and 1.2.14 implementations all free the primary PCM allocation even after a negative `hw_free`/plugin-close result. A negative result therefore records primary-handle consumption but is NOT a complete plugin/hardware-retirement receipt; that operation remains retained and blocks replacement/update admission. No invalid consumed pointer is retried. Native pipe-close failures and unexpected Arc/worker ownership also remain typed non-success. The global ALSA cached-configuration lifetime is preexisting and separate from the PCM receipt.

No new catalog probing is introduced. Device enumeration continues using ALSA direction hints. Only existing selected/default endpoint configuration/build operations open PCM. CString/config errors before native entry have no native fence. The documented negative return from `snd_pcm_open` rejects the operation without transferring a PCM to the application. Busy, missing-device, permission and unsupported-direction errors preserve their original error and may recover after the actual operation/control/TLS/supervisor joins. Rejection is recorded separately from acquired/checked-close state; it never synthesizes a successful PCM-close status or retries an invalid pointer. A blocked call, interrupted/unknown open phase, actual owned handle, native-close failure or worker panic remains retained and denies replacement.

This application receipt does not establish cleanup of arbitrary same-user native plugin/configuration code. A precise reviewed libasound 1.2.11 limitation is that `snd_pcm_hw_open_fd` has rare protocol-version/ioctl error returns after receiving an fd without closing it; the caller returns that error without a PCM ownership transfer. The application cannot safely identify or close such library-private descriptors. That residual library/target gate requires actual target acceptance and, for complete containment/recoverability of untrusted plugin internals, a separately reviewed process-owned audio endpoint; it does not justify disabling every ordinary returned open rejection. Standard hardware, PulseAudio and PipeWire plugin/device behavior remains unaccepted by source preparation.

## Consumers and verification

Separate Linux application DATA requires native receipts before call cleanup/route replacement, opener release, ringtone/PCM Permit release, attachment completion and ordinary-shutdown success. The exact PCM terminal-producer guard stays owned on failed close or panic; cancellation alone is never release authority. Windows and macOS contracts are unchanged and require their own receipts.

Focused existing-module regression sources cover actual callback/TLS joins, actual control/TLS joins through the hardware-free ALSA null plugin, typed negative-status retention, atomic callback revocation and actual Rust callback panic retention. They have not been executed as part of source preparation. Device/call/rejoin/attachment/update, target library/plugin versions, host installation and licensing/distribution acceptance remain open until independently reviewed fresh hosted evidence exists. Source inclusion and SPDX/license files do not imply complete corresponding-source, relink or legal acceptance.
